newsitem.title: USA: Tracor unit wins $26-mln Air Force contract.
newsitem.headline: Tracor unit wins $26-mln Air Force contract.

text.p: Aerospace Inc, a unit of Tracor Inc, said Monday it won a $26-million contract from the U.S. Air Force for production of the 525 AN/ALE-47 (V), an electronic countermeasure systems.

George Melton, president of Tracor Aerospace, said the contract provides a five-year production base, which, when combined with direct international sales, could ultimately exceed $50 million during the period.
Deliveries under the new contract are scheduled to commence in January 1998 and the contract is expected to be completed in September 2002, the Tracor unit said.

The AN/ALE-47, which Tracor Aerospace developed, is a flight-line software programmable system capable of dispensing chaff, flares, active radio-frequency decoys, and other expendables from military aircraft to improve survivavility of disabled aircraft.

The systems have been selected for installation in more than 15 aircraft types and are currently being installed on U.S. Air Force F-16, C-130, C-141, C-17, C-5, and E-8C aircraft; and U.S. Navy F/A-18, MV-22, P-3, and HH-60G/H aircraft.
The system is also being installed on U.S. Army MH-47D and MH-60L/K aircraft.
A Tracor spokeswoman said that the air forces of several other countries, including the United Kingdon, Japan, New Zealand, and Korea also use the system.
The unit said it has completed delivery of 1,069 systems under a previous contract with all deliveries on or ahead of schedule and is in the process of delivering 267 more systems.
